I am 70 this year, my legs are not what they used to be, but I still know every piece of my 10.1 mu. My father taught me to farm when I was 15, and I have done it this way ever since. I never went to school — everything I know, I learned by doing it and watching the neighbors. I work the land alone now. On 7 mu I do wheat in winter and then maize in summer, like everyone here. The other 3.1 mu I plant cotton — I keep it because the price from the buyer is alright and I know how to grow it. I have a well, so when the crops look thirsty, I water them.

For the wheat on those 7 mu: I buy the improved seeds from the shop in town, the same ones my nephew uses — his wheat always looks good. In October, before I sow, I run the rotary tiller over the ground. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer on each mu — that is four-fifths of a bag. When the wheat wakes up in spring and starts growing fast, I spread 80 jin of urea per mu, half when it turns green and half when it shoots up tall. I water three times: once when it wakes up from winter, once when it gets tall, and once when the grain fills. I spray for bugs twice. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, and I expect the same this year — about 450 kg.

For the maize: As soon as the wheat is cut in June, I plant the maize. I use hybrid seeds — everyone uses hybrid now, or you get nothing. I do not till again, I just sow directly into the wheat stubble with the machine because there is no time to waste. I put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. When the plants are knee-high, I spread 60 jin of urea per mu. I water twice, three times if the summer stays dry. Two sprays for bugs. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, so 500 kg.

For the cotton on the 3.1 mu: I plant in April. I use improved seeds. I till the soil first with the rotary tiller because cotton likes loose ground. I put a full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 100 jin, 50 kg. When the flowers come, I add 60 jin of urea per mu. I water three times. Cotton has more pests than grain, so I spray three times. Last year I got about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu, and I hope for the same — about 250 kg.

Why do I do it this way? Because this is what I did last year, and the year before, and it worked. My neighbor Old Wang does about the same. Fertilizer costs a lot of money, but if I use too little and the crop fails, I lose everything. At my age, I do not try new things. I watch what works and I copy it. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than sleep at night worrying about a bad harvest.
